questions.question: A cylinder and a cone have the same height and the same radius as that of their base. The ratio of the volume of the cone to the volume of the cylinder is:
questions.solution:

For a **cylinder** and a **cone** having the **same radius (r)** and **same height (h)**:

**Volume of Cylinder** = πr²h

**Volume of Cone** = (1/3) × πr²h

Ratio = **Volume of Cone** : **Volume of Cylinder** = (1/3) : 1 = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Radius** of cylinder = **Radius** of cone = r

⇒ **Height** of cylinder = **Height** of cone = h

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Volume of a Cylinder** = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Required Ratio = (Volume of Cone) / (Volume of Cylinder)

⇒ Ratio = [(1/3) × π × r² × h] / [π × r² × h]

⇒ Ratio = (1/3) / 1

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 800 is invested for 3 years at simple interest rate. The rates of interest for the 3 years are 6%, 8% and 10% per annum. Find the total amount of interest earned at the end of 3 years.

• The** Pacific ring of fire or the circum-Pacific belt** is another name for the Ring of Fire.
 
• **Volcanoes along that stretch of the Pacific Ocean are extremely active**, and earthquakes happen frequently there.
 
• The **majority of earthquakes and volcanic eruptions** are recorded in and near the Ring of Fire.
 
• It is roughly **40,000 km long**.
 
• **75% of Earth's volcanoes** are located along the Ring of Fire.
 
• The significant tectonic plates that surround the area are responsible for the** high frequency of earthquakes**.
 
• At convergent boundaries known as **subduction zones**, plates cross each other.
 
• They are related to **deep trenches**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pacific, Juan de Fuca, Cocos, Indian-Australian, Nazca, North American, and Philippine Plates **are just a few of the tectonic plates that it follows as it delineates boundaries between them.
 
• The Pacific Rim includes the western coasts of North and South America, as well as the coasts of Australia, eastern Asia, and the Pacific islands.
 
• The** majority of the planet's earthquakes**, including the most severe and dramatic seismic events, happen along its path.
 
• Two-thirds of all volcanoes in the world, or 850–1,000, are located in the Ring of Fire and have erupted recently.

• The** United Nations defines a nuclear-weapon-free zone (NWFZ) **as a free agreement reached by a group of states through a treaty or convention.
 
• It **forbids the development, production, control, possession, testing, stationing, or transportation of nuclear weapons **in a specific area.
 
• The NWFZ must also have mechanisms for** verification and control** to ensure that its obligations are upheld, and it must be recognised as such by the General Assembly of the UN.
 
• Although most nations, including **five nuclear-armed states**, are parties to the **Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons**, NWFZs serve a different purpose.
 
• **South Korea and Japan** are American allies that do not possess nuclear weapons.

• In a similar vein, the **2+4 Treaty**, which brought about **German reunification, prohibited nuclear weapons in the new states of Germany** (Berlin and former East Germany).

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as the first Vernacular newspaper of India?

• **Samachar Darpan**

 
 
• **Baptist Missionary** published the Samachar Darpan in** Serampore's Mission Press**.
 
• During** Lord Hastings' administration** (1813 to 1823), it was published.
 
• The **first vernacular newspaper in India was Samachar Darpan**, which was launched on **May 31, 1818**. 
 
• It is regarded as the **very first newspaper** published in the **Indian language**.
 
• It included news** primarily from English newspapers**, but it also included news from other sources.
 
• The newspaper covered the following topics:** births, deaths, and obituaries; government news; news of government officials; news of other European nations besides Britain**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Madras Courier was **one of the first newspapers in India and the first to be published in Madras, Madras Presidency,** and British India.
 
• Published on** October 12, 1785, it was the top publication** at the time and the one that the government officially designated for printing official notices.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Gazette**
 
 
• The** English-language weekly newspaper** Hicky's Bengal Gazette was published in **Kolkata (then Calcutta)**, the nation's capital of British India.
 
• Between **1780 and 1782, it was the first newspaper printed in Asia** and was in circulation for two years before the East India Company seized the newspaper's printing press and types.

• Butane is a hydrocarbon that can be easily liquefied and is a highly **flammable, colourless, and odourless gas**.
